legend: There is a sheet of paper that can be represented with a grid of size n×m%%ZSMJ0%%: n%%ZSMJ1%% rows and m%%ZSMJ2%% columns of cells. All cells are colored in white initially.
q%%ZSMJ3%% operations have been applied to the sheet. The i%%ZSMJ4%%-th of them can be described as follows:

xi%%ZSMJ5%% yi%%ZSMJ6%% — choose one of k%%ZSMJ7%% non-white colors and color the entire row xi%%ZSMJ8%% and the entire column yi%%ZSMJ9%% in it. The new color is applied to each cell, regardless of whether the cell was colored before the operation.
The sheet after applying all q%%ZSMJ10%% operations is called a coloring. Two colorings are different if there exists at least one cell that is colored in different colors.
How many different colorings are there? Print the number modulo 998244353%%ZSMJ11%%.
input: The first line contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ12%% (1≤t≤104%%ZSMJ13%%) — the number of testcases.
The first line of the testcase contains four integers n,m,k%%ZSMJ14%% and q%%ZSMJ15%% (1≤n,m,k,q≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ16%%) — the size of the sheet, the number of non-white colors and the number of operations.

The i%%ZSMJ17%%-th of the following q%%ZSMJ18%% lines contains a description of the i%%ZSMJ19%%-th operation — two integers xi%%ZSMJ20%% and yi%%ZSMJ21%% (1≤xi≤n%%ZSMJ22%%; 1≤yi≤m%%ZSMJ23%%) — the row and the column the operation is applied to.
The sum of q%%ZSMJ24%% over all testcases doesn't exceed 2⋅105%%ZSMJ25%%.
output: For each testcase, print a single integer — the number of different colorings modulo 998244353%%ZSMJ26%%.
